newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX overcomes rate woe, rises with dollar.
newsitem.headline: German DAX overcomes rate woe, rises with dollar.

text.p: German shares posted modest gains in thinly-traded bourse dealings on Wednesday, as the dollar's continued ascent against the mark helped push prices higher late in the session.

The blue-chip DAX index climbed 32.71 points, or 0.8 percent, to 4,335.39 points, clocking up the bulk of gains just before the session close as the dollar briefly rose above an eight-year high of 1.89 marks.
Seven of the 30 blue-chip stocks fell while the rest advanced.
Dealers said the dollar's advance, always good news for Germany's U.S.-dependent exporters, had offset persistent worries about a possible interest rate hike by the Bundesbank.
In addition, a report showing the German seasonally-adjusted unemployment total had risen by a stronger than expected 17,000 in July appeared to argue against an imminent rate rise.
"It's a fairly uncertain picture but people seem to have decided to take their tune from the strong dollar right at present," said a dealer.
There was little evidence of a strong trend.

Bank shares, the outperformers for weeks, suffered the heaviest losses. Isolated big-ticket shares, such as Siemens which rose 2.50 marks to 123.80 marks on healthy volumes, carried the market higher.
Sportswear manufacturer Adidas got an early boost after it reported that its first-half profit jumped to 238 million marks from 184 million marks -- at the top end of forecasts.
The shares hit a high of 223 marks in IBIS trade before settling back to end at 218 marks, up two marks.
